title: Temperature × pressure MatterSim Mirror factor (synthetic condition-invariance screen)
hypothesis: A compact T×P code adds useful condition-specific force-law capacity beyond one shared potential and native direct condition scalars, while preserving force consistency and improving actual bytes/quality.
mirror_coordinate: Separable temperature and pressure code factors

development.selection_metric: development-only check of separable rank-1 T×P code against native condition table

success_gate: On condition-shifted heldout ensembles, Mirror improves combined energy/force error at >=25% fewer actual bytes than direct native T/P conditioning, with conservative force and rotation equivariance checks passing.
failure_gate: Shared condition-invariant potential is sufficient, Mirror exactly aliases native condition controls without improving the Pareto frontier, or physical consistency fails.
boundaries: Synthetic Lennard-Jones condition-sampling screen only; not MatterSim, not PA299 reproduction, and not an NPT benchmark.
T/P change sampled geometry distribution; the physical pair potential is held fixed by construction.
This screen tests whether condition codes are needed to change the force law, not MatterSim's ensemble accuracy.
decision: Scoped synthetic FAIL: shared condition-invariant potential is exact and Mirror codes add bytes/compute.
